section: Juvenile Justice Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment 2016
subsections: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions
Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: The 2016 amendment to the child labour law came into force on:
accepted.x: The 2016 amendment came into force on 1 September 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the amendment year from its date of commencement.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the age categories under the amended child labour law:
1. A child is a person below 14 years of age.
2. An adolescent is a person between 14 and 18 years of age.
3. The category of adolescent was introduced only through the 2016 amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 2016 amendment introduced the adolescent category for persons aged 14 to 18 years.
accepted.tq: Use the age table and identify the newly introduced category.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a child below 14 years after the 2016 amendment?
o: Employment is banned in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions
Employment is banned only in mines and factories
Employment is permitted in all non-hazardous occupations without restriction
Employment is regulated only through the Right to Education Act
accepted.x: After the 2016 amendment, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.
accepted.tq: Separate the post-amendment blanket prohibition from the earlier listed-work model.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Before the 2016 amendment, the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 provided that children below 14 years could not be employed in:
o: Only the occupations and processes listed in the Act
accepted.x: The 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in listed occupations and processes, while work elsewhere was regulated rather than completely prohibited.
accepted.tq: Compare the limited prohibition under the original law with the later wider prohibition.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: The original 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in how many occupations and processes, respectively?
accepted.x: The original law listed 18 prohibited occupations and 65 prohibited processes for children below 14 years.
accepted.tq: Match the two numerical components without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the principal hazardous categories retained after the 2016 amendment?
o: Hazardous processes under the Factories Act
accepted.x: The retained hazardous categories are mines, inflammable substances and explosives, and hazardous processes under the Factories Act. All agricultural occupations are not included as a category of the hazardous list.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the narrowed hazardous list.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Which authority may add or omit occupations from the hazardous list under the amended child labour law?
accepted.x: The Centre may add occupations to, or omit occupations from, the hazardous list.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who has the power’ method to identify the competent authority.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: A child assists in the family enterprise after school hours, and the activity does not affect schooling. Under the amended law, this situation is generally treated as:
o: A specified exception to the prohibition
Permissible only if the child is above 18 years
Permissible only in mines and factories
accepted.x: Helping in a family or family enterprise after school hours is a specified exception, provided the conditions relating to schooling are satisfied.
accepted.tq: Apply the exception to a short factual situation rather than memorising it in isolation.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the exception relating to child artists?
o: A child may work in any circus without restriction if accompanied by a parent
A child artist is exempt even when schooling is affected
A child may work only in theatrical entertainment and not in audio-visual entertainment
A child may work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment, excluding circus, if schooling is not affected
accepted.x: The exception covers a child artist in audio-visual entertainment but excludes circus work and requires that schooling should not be affected.
accepted.tq: Separate the permitted audio-visual exception from the expressly excluded circus activity.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding enforcement and penalties under the amended child labour law:
1. Offences under the Act are cognizable.
2. The penalty may include imprisonment from six months to two years.
3. The fine may range from ₹20,000 to ₹50,000.
4. The Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The amendment made offences cognizable, prescribed imprisonment and fines, and provided for a Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund.
accepted.tq: Combine legal character, punishment figures and institutional provisions in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: The primary responsibility for enforcement of the amended child labour law is vested in the:
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
accepted.x: Enforcement powers under the amended framework rest with the District Magistrate.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-power trap by identifying the designated enforcement authority.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: The Amendment Rules relating to the amended child labour law were notified in:
accepted.x: The Amendment Rules were notified in 2017 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the amendment from the year of the rules.
accepted.sec: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

accepted.s: Under the Juvenile Justice framework, children in conflict with law are dealt with by the:
o: Children's Court in every case at the first instance
District Magistrate acting as a criminal court
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Board handles matters concerning children in conflict with law. A Children's Court tries cases transferred to it under the statutory procedure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the body dealing with children in conflict with law from the body dealing with care and protection.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: A Juvenile Justice Board consists of:
o: A Sessions Judge and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers, at least one of whom is a woman
A Chairperson and four members, all of whom must be social workers
A District Magistrate and five elected representatives
accepted.x: The Board comprises a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class serving as Principal Magistrate and two social workers, with at least one woman among the social workers.
accepted.tq: Test composition by separating the judicial member from the social-worker members.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Juvenile Justice Board from the Children's Court?
o: The Children's Court deals only with children requiring care and protection
The Board handles children in conflict with law, while the Children's Court tries cases transferred to it
The Board tries all transferred cases, while the Children's Court conducts preliminary inquiries only
Both bodies have identical jurisdiction in every case
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Board handles children in conflict with law, whereas the Children's Court, a Sessions Court, tries cases transferred to it.
accepted.tq: Compare jurisdiction and identify the body assigned the transferred trial.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: The guiding principle in inquiries and proceedings involving children under the Juvenile Justice system is:
o: Best interests of the child through child-friendly and rehabilitation-oriented justice
Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective
accepted.x: The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.
accepted.tq: Identify the governing principle from the stated purpose of the legal process.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the functioning of Juvenile Justice Boards in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Boards were functioning in the erstwhile 13 districts.
2. Selection was undertaken for Child Welfare Committees and Juvenile Justice Boards in the 13 new districts.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Juvenile Welfare Department also implements the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh had Boards in the erstwhile 13 districts, undertook selection for bodies in the 13 new districts, and its Juvenile Welfare Department also runs the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
accepted.tq: Combine administrative structure, reorganisation and departmental responsibility.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: Each Child Welfare Committee in Andhra Pradesh consists of:
o: A District Magistrate and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers
accepted.x: Each Child Welfare Committee consists of one Chairperson and four members.
accepted.tq: Avoid confusing the composition of a Child Welfare Committee with that of a Juvenile Justice Board.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: During the financial year 2025–26, the Child Welfare Committees in Andhra Pradesh handled and disposed of cases in which of the following numbers?
accepted.x: The Committees handled 4,189 cases and disposed of 3,691 cases during FY 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Keep the figures in their functional order: cases handled first and cases disposed second.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

accepted.s: How many children were declared legally free for adoption by the Child Welfare Committees in Andhra Pradesh during FY 2025–26?
accepted.x: During FY 2025–26, 55 children were declared legally free for adoption.
accepted.tq: Select the adoption-related figure rather than the larger case-disposal figures.
accepted.sec: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning
